verdicts.reason: A keeps the headline prominent on the left, but the middle is a mess: the logo is squashed into a column with an avatar and emojis floating loose, the right-side chat bubbles and the feedback copy are too small to read, a pink blob leaves a big dead area, and the logo sits tiny at the far right. B is worse: the subordinate feedback copy is the biggest text and outranks the tiny headline, chat bubbles are empty and cut off by the blob, avatars and emojis are split from their speech, the text sits on shapes, and the whole thing reads as scattered pieces.
